result.question:
/design:design-system  please research how other monorepo TUI works, if they have any. 

Also research TUIs for other things, well known TUIs. How they behave, how they interact, how they provide feedback. Save this research in the documents for us to use as inspiration and improvements source for smith. You can create a “tui-research” folder inside smith folder so you can access it and run the TUIs you install to test. 

Take screenshots, navigate the TUIs and really extract the inspiration from the best TUIs
result.summary: Monorepo TUIs exist but are few. Nx (21+) and Turborepo (2.0) ship terminal UIs built around a task list plus a per-task output pane, with pinning and the ability to enter an interactive task. Nx Console is an editor GUI, not a TUI. Well-known general TUIs (lazygit, k9s, lazydocker, yazi, btop) show a live-updating, keyboard-first pattern worth copying. The research also yielded a practical method for capturing TUI screenshots (VHS tapes, testty PTY driving, approved-baseline regression) and design rules (build hierarchy before color, reserve intense styling for state changes). Hands-on screenshots and navigation of installed TUIs were not part of the verified evidence, so that work remains to be done.

findings.claim: Nx and Turborepo both ship real terminal UIs for monorepo task running. Nx Console, however, is an IDE GUI and not a TUI.
findings.evidence: Nx Console README: UI for Nx & Lerna in VS Code, Cursor and JetBrains (3-0). Nx TUI and Turborepo 2.0 TUI are separate terminal products. A general comparison article does not cover TUIs at all (3-0), so use primary docs for monorepo TUI research.

findings.claim: Nx TUI pattern: aimed at continuous, long-running tasks (dev servers, watch libs). Users pin tasks, see live output, and use interactive sub-terminals.
findings.evidence: Video page chapters 'Pinning and inspecting tasks' and 'Interactive sub-terminals'. Verifiers noted the TUI also covers ordinary build/test runs, pinning is capped at two tasks, and Windows was disabled in the initial Nx 21 release.

findings.claim: Turborepo 2.0 TUI pattern: task sidebar on the left, main pane shows the selected task's logs, so logs are read per task instead of interleaved.
findings.evidence: Article describes tasks on the left and task details in the main window, with logs explored individually. A related claim about stdin via persistent tasks and Enter/Ctrl+Z was refuted (0-3), so do not cite it. The layout rests on a blog, not Turborepo's own docs.

findings.claim: Well-known general TUIs worth studying: lazygit (about 79.2K stars, keystroke-driven staging/branching/rebasing) and k9s (live view that refreshes as the cluster changes). The star-history roundup also lists lazydocker, yazi, btop, Posting.
findings.evidence: Roundup dated 2026-06-30 gives the star table and calls lazygit the poster child of GUI defection. k9s real-time watching is also confirmed by k9scli.io per a verifier. Feedback model to borrow: auto-refreshing live state, not manual refresh.

findings.claim: Screenshot capture method: VHS tape scripts drive a TUI and take PNGs with Screenshot <path>, synced with Wait+Screen@<timeout> /<regex>/. testty compiles a PTY scenario into a VHS tape and also drives a real TUI in a PTY with vt100 state capture.
findings.evidence: vhs.rs maps Capture to Screenshot and WaitForText to Wait+Screen (3-0). testty docs confirm PTY driving with vt100 (3-0). One claim about testty producing pixel-accurate images through its own renderer was refuted (1-2), so rely on VHS for pixels.

findings.claim: Screenshot regression pattern from Netclaw: a screenshots profile captures PNGs of stable TUI states via VHS, with determinism pinned (CursorBlink false, pinned theme, pinned VHS checksum). Each PNG is compared byte-for-byte (cmp) against a committed approved baseline. A missing baseline or a mismatch saves the actual image plus an ImageMagick diff and fails.
findings.evidence: Verifier read the PR body and the run-smoke.sh diff. Diff PNG is produced only if ImageMagick compare is installed. CursorBlink detail rests on the PR body, not the tape file.

findings.claim: Documentation capture choices: a static screenshot is the quickest default. asciinema is a live capture (you drive keys) with agg converting cast to GIF. VHS is the scripted, fully automated alternative.
findings.evidence: triage-tui demo README: static assets/demo.png is the default, animated recording is an optional upgrade.

findings.claim: Visual design rules for TUIs: build hierarchy in order placement, spacing, grouping, text labels, alignment, weight, then color, and never let color carry the whole hierarchy. Reserve high-intensity color, heavy borders, inverse video, animation and icons for state changes or actions.
findings.evidence: Quotes match the skill text. It is one author's heuristic in a marketplace listing, but consistent with WCAG 1.4.1, NO_COLOR and pairing color with symbols and bold/dim, per a verifier.

findings.claim: Framework models: Bubble Tea uses the Elm Architecture (Model, Init, Update, View, with messages and optional commands). Ratatui is immediate-mode, the app owns the loop and describes the whole UI each frame. A Sparkles design note recommends immediate mode as default with optional retained and incremental paths.
findings.evidence: Bubble Tea and Ratatui claims were 3-0 and backed by their primary docs per verifiers. The Sparkles recommendation was 2-1 and is a design opinion for a D-language library, not a general finding. Ratatui still diffs buffers at terminal output level.

findings.claim: The awesome-tuis directory article is thin for this question. It does not cover feedback design or monorepo TUIs and gives no freshness indicators. A claim that it names specific TUIs to test was refuted (0-3).
findings.evidence: Verifiers found no feedback-design or monorepo content. Use the rothgar/awesome-tuis repo directly for candidates instead of this article.

result.caveats: The verified claims are mostly secondary sources (blogs, video pages, a skills listing). The Turborepo layout rests on one blog. Nx TUI details come from a video page, with Nx docs only noted by a verifier. No claim covers behavior or feedback of the TUIs from hands-on use. The user asked for installs, screenshots and navigation in a tui-research folder, and none of that is evidenced here. Refuted claims (Nx vs Turborepo output capture, testty pixel renderer, Turborepo stdin flow) are excluded. Windows support for the Nx TUI was disabled at launch, and several sources date from 2024-2025 and may have changed.

refuted.claim: Nx (per its own docs) preserves native terminal output (spinners, colors, animations) while Turborepo output has none of these.
Turborepo captures task output only via piping, which the page says breaks tools with rich output such as Cypress and webpack; Nx supports other capture strategies.
testty generates screenshots via a VHS tape compiler and a renderer that produces pixel-accurate terminal images.
Turborepo 2.0 TUI tasks can take stdin input: mark a task persistent: true in turbo.json, select it, press Enter to enter its shell, and Ctrl+Z to exit.
The list names well-known dev TUIs that serve as candidates to test for smith: lazygit, gitui, k9s, lazydocker, btop++, bottom, helix, yazi, lazysql, posting.
